claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing a gradient microstructure will enhance room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated material.
Introducing a gradient microstructure will maintain or increase strength relative to the untreated material.
The proposed gradient transitions from fine to coarse microstructural features.
The proposed performance comparison is under room-temperature tensile testing in standard laboratory conditions.
The gradient microstructure reduces dislocation pile-ups.
A smoother transition in microstructural features distributes stress more evenly.
The gradient microstructure mitigates local stress concentrations.
The gradient microstructure is predicted to increase ductility by approximately 20% relative to the untreated material.
The gradient microstructure is predicted to maintain or increase strength relative to the untreated material.
The untreated material has limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Brittleness in the untreated material leads to catastrophic failure under stress.
The hypothesis is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The proposed effect may not generalize to other alloy systems or microstructures.
The magnitude of ductility improvement and strength retention depends on the specific gradient design.
